# lowering

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/lowering"
```

Package lowering replaces checked expressions with equivalent Go statements.

The [checker](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/checker/readme.md>) supplies syntax, types, bindings, and operation records. LowerPropagations handles propagation, if values, and comprehensions. It returns formatted file contents; the [driver](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/driver/readme.md>) writes them to owned generated paths.

### Calls and branches

For use\(first\(\), target\(\)\!, last\(\)\), save first before calling target once. If target fails, return before last or use runs. Preserve the order Go defines; do not impose order where Go leaves it unspecified. For left\(\) && right\(\)\!, evaluate right and check its error only on the true path of left.

An if value uses a result local and ordinary branches:

```
var chosen string
if ok {
    log("yes")
    chosen = "yes"
} else {
    chosen = "no"
}
name := chosen
```

A branch that returns or jumps out needs no result assignment. Returns, defers, and jumps keep their source function and targets.

A comprehension uses one result collection and direct nested range loops. Filters enclose later clauses. Each accepted slice value is appended; map keys and values are saved in that order before insertion. A simple slice or array range can allocate its exact result length and write by range index. Returns, defers, and jumps remain in their source function.

### Errors and saved types

Check the original error before return conversion. A nil concrete pointer can become a non\-nil error interface if converted first. An error interface that already contains a nil pointer is failure. Generic error checks use reflection when direct nil comparison is unavailable.

\! returns the same error; \!\! adds call\-name context with %w in the failure branch. Other results get typed zero values. Result names and source defers retain their meaning.

Save values with checked types and fresh names. For example, var saved uint64 = 1 \<\< n retains its source conversion; inferred int could change the result. Print types by object identity. Required types must be accessible in the generated scope. Fresh import aliases avoid source names.

### Loops and storage

Keep conditions at each loop visit. Run post work after the first visit; continue must still reach it. An if value in a loop initializer can break or continue that loop. Preserve separate := iteration variables and closure bindings when generated control flow requires renaming.

In selects, evaluate channel and send operands before selection. Evaluate receive\-assignment destinations only inside the selected case.

Record assignment destinations without reading them, evaluate right\-hand values, then store. Keep the original array or evaluated slice and map. A later store panic must not move ahead of an earlier propagation return.

InsertAfter is a separate ordinary\-Go API; see the [public API](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/pkg/transpiler/readme.md>) for use. Both operations copy changed syntax without modifying checked input, so one load can support independent rewrites. [Tests](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/tests/readme.md>) compare execution with handwritten references; valid Go alone does not prove equivalent behavior.

## type Site

Site identifies an expression in the original source. Offsets are bytes.

```go
type Site struct {
    File         string `json:"file"`
    Start        int    `json:"start"`
    End          int    `json:"end"`
    Kind         string `json:"kind"`
    Reason       string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
    ErrorReturn  bool   `json:"error_return"`
    ReturnReason string `json:"return_reason,omitempty"`
}
```

## type Source

Source contains the original syntax and its type information.

```go
type Source struct {
    Package *packages.Package

    Sites []Site
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Load

```go
func Load(dir, pattern string) (*Source, error)
```

Load reads and type\-checks one Go package selected by pattern in dir. It records expression positions for later statement insertion.

### func SourceFromCheckedPackage

```go
func SourceFromCheckedPackage(p *checker.Package, dir string) (*Source, error)
```

SourceFromCheckedPackage records expressions from private source checking.

### func SourceFromPackage

```go
func SourceFromPackage(p *packages.Package, dir string) (*Source, error)
```

SourceFromPackage records expression positions and insertion limits in a checked package. File names are relative to dir; a package with type errors returns an error.

### func \(\*Source\) InsertAfter

```go
func (s *Source) InsertAfter(site Site, after After) (map[string][]byte, error)
```

InsertAfter returns Go files with the callback's statements after the selected expression. The callback receives saved results; the original syntax tree stays unchanged.

### func \(\*Source\) LowerPropagations

```go
func (s *Source) LowerPropagations(operations map[string]Propagation) (map[string][]byte, error)
```

LowerPropagations replaces checked propagation, if values, and comprehensions with ordinary Go. It returns formatted file contents by absolute path without writing files. It reports an error if any accepted operation was not replaced.
